notes.front: What is Azure SQL?
notes.back: A collective name for Microsoft’s family of database services in Azure that are based on SQL Server.
notes.explanation: The family spans a range of control, from a virtual machine you manage yourself to fully managed database services.
notes.example: Like a car maker’s range of one engine in different bodies, but here one database engine offered with different amounts of management done for you.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines?
notes.back: Full versions of SQL Server installed on virtual machines in Azure, with no on-premises hardware to manage.
notes.explanation: You get the same product you would run in your own data centre, only on Azure’s hardware.
notes.example: Like renting an empty flat: the building is Azure’s, but you furnish it and look after everything inside, including the server and database software.
introduces: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is SQL Server on Azure Windows Virtual Machines?, “Overview”
notes.evidence: enables you to use full versions of SQL Server in the cloud without having to manage any on-premises hardware.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?
notes.back: A platform as a service offering with near 100% compatibility with the latest Enterprise Edition SQL Server Database Engine.
notes.explanation: It is platform as a service, yet a close match for the engine of SQL Server’s latest Enterprise Edition.
notes.example: Like moving your whole office, filing system and all, into a serviced building where the landlord handles repairs and security.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?, “Overview”
notes.evidence: Azure SQL Managed Instance is a PaaS service that has near 100% compatibility with the latest Enterprise Edition SQL Server Database Engine.

notes.front: What is Azure SQL Database?
notes.back: A fully managed platform as a service database engine that handles upgrading, patching, backups and monitoring without user involvement.
notes.explanation: The sql-docs say it handles most of the database management functions, so you work on the database rather than the server.
notes.example: Like a hotel room rather than a flat: you bring only your belongings (the data), and everything else is looked after.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “What is Azure SQL Database?”
notes.evidence: Azure SQL Database, a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS) database engine that handles most of the database management functions such as upgrading, patching, backups, and monitoring without user involvement.

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, what is a logical server?
notes.back: A logical construct that acts as the central administrative point for a group of single or pooled databases.
notes.explanation: Settings such as logins, firewall rules, auditing rules and failover groups are managed there for the databases it holds.
notes.example: Like a school office that keeps the registers, keys and rules for several classrooms, without being a classroom itself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Azure SQL Database”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, what is a single database?
notes.back: A fully managed, isolated database with its own dedicated resources.
notes.explanation: The sql-docs suggest it for modern cloud applications and microservices that need a single reliable data source.
notes.example: Like a detached house: its own plot and its own utilities, shared with no neighbours.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Deployment models”
notes.evidence: Single database represents a fully managed, isolated database. You might use this option if you have modern cloud applications and microservices that need a single reliable data source.

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, what is an elastic pool?
notes.back: A group of databases on a single server that share a set amount of resources at a set price.
notes.explanation: The sql-docs describe it as a cost-effective way to manage and scale many databases whose demand varies unpredictably.
notes.example: Like a family mobile plan: everyone draws on one shared allowance, and whoever is busy this week uses more of it.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Elastic pools help you manage and scale multiple databases in Azure SQL Database, “Elastic pools”
notes.evidence: Azure SQL Database elastic pools are a simple, cost-effective solution for managing and scaling multiple databases with varying and unpredictable usage demands. The databases in an elastic pool are on a single server and share a set number of resources at a set price.

notes.front: What is the Hyperscale service tier of Azure SQL Database?
notes.back: A tier for customers who need higher performance and availability, fast backup and restore, and fast storage and compute scaling.
notes.explanation: Speed of backup, restore and scaling is what the tier offers those customers.
notes.example: Like a warehouse whose walls move outwards as stock arrives, instead of one built to a fixed size on day one.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Hyperscale service tier, “Who should consider the Hyperscale service tier”
notes.evidence: The Hyperscale service tier is intended for all customers who require higher performance and availability, fast backup and restore, and fast storage and compute scalability.

notes.front: What is Data Migration Assistant (DMA)?
notes.back: A tool that analyses your SQL Server databases and reports issues that could block or affect a move to Azure SQL.
notes.explanation: The training still names it for checking compatibility before a move, but Microsoft retired DMA on 16 July 2025 and now points to other migration tools.
notes.example: Like a removals firm’s survey visit that lists the items too big for the new house before moving day.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, what is point-in-time restore?
notes.back: Recovering a database to any point in time within the automatic backup retention period.
notes.explanation: Every SQL Database deployment option supports it, for any database.
notes.example: Like a document’s version history that lets you reopen it exactly as it stood at 10:42 last Tuesday.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Availability capabilities”
notes.evidence: All SQL Database deployment options support recovery to any point in time within the automatic backup retention period for any database.

notes.front: What is SQL database in Fabric?
notes.back: A developer-friendly transactional database in Microsoft Fabric, based on Azure SQL Database, for creating operational databases in Fabric.
notes.explanation: It brings an Azure SQL Database-style operational database into the Fabric platform.
notes.example: Like a familiar shop opening a branch inside a shopping centre: the same stock, but now part of the centre’s shared services.
notes.source: Fabric docs (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs): SQL database in Microsoft Fabric, “SQL database in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.evidence: SQL database in Microsoft Fabric is a developer-friendly transactional database, based on Azure SQL Database, that allows you to easily create your operational database in Fabric.

notes.front: Which Azure SQL product keeps 100% SQL Server compatibility and gives operating system-level access?
notes.back: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines.
notes.explanation: Microsoft pitches it as lift-and-shift with ease while keeping full SQL Server compatibility.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL?, “Azure SQL”
notes.evidence: Lift-and-shift your SQL Server workloads with ease and maintain 100% SQL Server compatibility and operating system-level access.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Which Azure SQL product does Microsoft call best for most migrations to the cloud?
notes.back: Azure SQL Managed Instance.
notes.explanation: It is a fully managed instance with almost 100% feature parity with the SQL Server database engine.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL?, “Azure SQL”
notes.evidence: with almost 100% feature parity with the SQL Server database engine. Best for most migrations to the cloud.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Which Azure SQL product is best for modern cloud applications that want the latest stable SQL Server features and face time pressure?
notes.back: Azure SQL Database.
notes.explanation: The docs pitch it at teams building new cloud applications under time pressure.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL?, “Azure SQL Database”
notes.evidence: Best for modern cloud applications that want to use the latest stable SQL Server features and have time constraints in development and marketing.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: With SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines, who decides when the operating system and database software are updated?
notes.back: You do: you have full control over the operating system and the SQL Server instance configuration.
notes.explanation: The same control means installing extra software, such as anti-virus, is also your decision.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL?, “Administration”
notes.evidence: With **SQL Server on Azure VMs**, you have full control over the operating system and SQL Server instance configuration. With a VM, it's up to you to decide when to update/upgrade the operating system and database software and when to install any extra software such as anti-virus.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Why is SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines a good fit for lift-and-shift migration?
notes.back: It is fully compatible with on-premises SQL Server, so applications and databases can move without change.
notes.explanation: Moving to an Azure virtual machine is much like moving databases from one on-premises server to another.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: How can SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines help with development and testing?
notes.back: You can set up development and test environments quickly without buying on-premises, non-production SQL Server hardware.
notes.explanation: The training also notes that an Azure virtual machine can be resized quickly without reinstalling its software.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: How can SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines extend an on-premises application?
notes.back: In a hybrid deployment: part of the system stays on-premises while its database elements run in the cloud.
notes.explanation: The training notes that the same server products, development tools and expertise work across both environments.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: A firm must move a legacy application to Azure within a month, unchanged. Its database relies on a third-party agent installed on the server’s operating system. Which option fits?
notes.back: D: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines.
notes.choices:
A) Azure SQL Database
B) SQL database in Fabric
C) Azure SQL Managed Instance
D) SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
notes.choicesExplained: A and C: they are platform as a service offerings, which do not give access to the server’s operating system. B: it is a Fabric database based on Azure SQL Database, with no operating system to install agents on.
notes.explanation: Only the virtual machine option gives operating system-level access, and it is lift-and-shift ready for fast migration with minimal or no changes.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL?, “Service comparison”
notes.evidence: Best for migrations and applications that require OS-level access. SQL virtual machines in Azure are lift-and-shift ready for existing applications that require fast migration to the cloud with minimal changes or no changes.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Which platform capabilities does Azure SQL Managed Instance take care of for you?
notes.back: Automatic patching and version updates, automated backups, and high availability.
notes.explanation: Handing these over drastically reduces management overhead and the total cost of ownership.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?, “Overview”
notes.evidence: At the same time, SQL Managed Instance provides all PaaS capabilities (automatic patching and version updates, automated backups, high availability) to drastically reduce management overhead and the total cost of ownership (TCO).

notes.front: How much change does moving on-premises applications to Azure SQL Managed Instance usually need?
notes.back: Minimal application and database changes.
notes.explanation: The docs aim it at existing SQL Server customers who want to lift and shift.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?, “Overview”
notes.evidence: SQL Managed Instance enables existing SQL Server customers to lift and shift their on-premises applications to the cloud with minimal application and database changes.

notes.front: Can one Azure SQL Managed Instance hold several databases?
notes.back: Yes: you can install multiple databases on the same instance, much as on an on-premises server.
notes.explanation: An instance is a whole SQL Server in the cloud, not a single database.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Azure SQL Managed Instance”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A retailer runs one on-premises SQL Server instance with 30 databases that use advanced SQL Server features. It wants to move them all to Azure with minimal changes and stop patching servers. Which option fits best?
notes.back: D: Azure SQL Managed Instance.
notes.choices:
A) SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
B) Azure SQL Database single databases
C) A new SQL Server in its own data centre
D) Azure SQL Managed Instance
notes.choicesExplained: A: a virtual machine would keep the patching work the retailer wants to drop. B: Azure SQL Database lacks some SQL Server features that on-premises applications may depend on. C: that keeps all the server management in-house.
notes.explanation: It accepts a whole SQL Server instance with its databases and offers compatibility with SQL Server.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?, “Overview”
notes.evidence: customers can lift and shift their existing SQL Server database or SQL Server instance to Azure SQL Managed Instance, which offers compatibility with SQL Server and complete isolation of customer instances with native VNet support.
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Is Azure SQL Database fully compatible with on-premises SQL Server?
notes.back: No. It supports most core database-level capabilities, but some features an on-premises application depends on may be missing.
notes.explanation: The training notes it is often used in new cloud projects, where the design can absorb any changes needed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: According to Microsoft’s training, what are two kinds of workload Azure SQL Database is often used for?
notes.back: Two of: modern cloud applications needing the latest stable features, applications that need high availability, and systems with variable load.
notes.explanation: For variable load, the server can scale up and down quickly without a costly manual upgrade.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A start-up is building a brand-new web application in the cloud. It wants the latest SQL Server features, the lowest administration and no servers to look after. Which option fits best?
notes.back: A: Azure SQL Database.
notes.choices:
A) Azure SQL Database
B) SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
C) Azure SQL Managed Instance with 30 databases
D) SQL Server installed on office hardware
notes.choicesExplained: B: a virtual machine leaves the operating system and database software for the start-up to manage. C: Managed Instance is aimed at migrating existing SQL Server estates. D: this means buying and running servers.
notes.explanation: It is designed for new cloud applications and offers low cost with minimal administration.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Are a single database’s compute, memory and storage shared with other databases?
notes.back: No. Each single database has its own guaranteed resources, dedicated to it alone.
notes.explanation: Isolation also makes each single database portable, and you can scale its resources up and down.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Scalable performance and pools”
notes.evidence: With single databases, each database is isolated from others and is portable. Each database has its own guaranteed amount of compute, memory, and storage resources. The resources you assign to the database are dedicated to that database and aren't shared with other databases in Azure.

notes.front: Which usage pattern suits an elastic pool?
notes.back: Many databases with low average use and infrequent spikes. Databases with persistent medium-high use should not share a pool.
notes.explanation: The docs contrast this with databases that stay busy, which should not be pooled together.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Elastic pools help you manage and scale multiple databases in Azure SQL Database, “When to consider a SQL Database elastic pool?”
notes.evidence: Pools are well suited for a large number of databases with specific utilization patterns. This pattern is characterized by low average utilization with infrequent utilization spikes for a given database. Conversely, multiple databases with persistent medium-high utilization shouldn't be placed in the same elastic pool.

notes.front: How is an elastic pool billed?
notes.back: By the hour for the pool itself, at its highest provisioned size, whatever the use; there is no per-database charge.
notes.explanation: You pay for the shared resources, so adding databases to the pool does not add a charge of its own.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Elastic pools help you manage and scale multiple databases in Azure SQL Database, “What are SQL elastic pools?”
notes.evidence: There's no per-database charge for elastic pools. You're billed for each hour a pool exists at the highest eDTU or vCores, regardless of usage or whether the pool was active for less than an hour.

notes.front: A software firm gives each of its 300 small customers their own database. Each is mostly idle but busy for short, unpredictable bursts. How should it deploy them in Azure SQL Database?
notes.back: A: in an elastic pool.
notes.choices:
A) In an elastic pool
B) As 300 single databases, each sized for its average
C) On one virtual machine per customer
D) As 300 single databases, each sized for its peak
notes.choicesExplained: D: sizing every database for its peak means paying for capacity that sits idle. B: sizing for the average leaves each one short during its bursts. C: 300 virtual machines add management work and do not share resources.
notes.explanation: Pools suit many databases with low average use and occasional spikes, sharing resources within a predictable budget.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Elastic pools help you manage and scale multiple databases in Azure SQL Database, “What are SQL elastic pools?”
notes.evidence: Elastic pools solve this problem by ensuring that databases get the performance resources they need when they need them. They provide a simple resource allocation mechanism within a predictable budget.

notes.front: A council’s booking app uses one database with a steady, predictable load, and must not share resources with anything else. Which Azure SQL Database option fits?
notes.back: D: a single database.
notes.choices:
A) SQL database in Fabric
B) An elastic pool
C) A logical server with no databases
D) A single database
notes.choicesExplained: B: a pool shares resources among databases, which the council does not want. C: a logical server only administers databases; it holds no data itself. A: that is a Fabric database, not an Azure SQL Database option.
notes.explanation: A single database is isolated with dedicated resources, and a predictable load is easy to size for.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Scalable performance and pools”
notes.evidence: Each database has its own guaranteed amount of compute, memory, and storage resources. The resources you assign to the database are dedicated to that database and aren't shared with other databases in Azure.

notes.front: How large can a single database in the Hyperscale service tier grow?
notes.back: Up to 128 terabytes.
notes.explanation: The training gives up to 100 terabytes, which the sql-docs now give as the limit for a Hyperscale elastic pool; a single database can reach 128.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Hyperscale service tier, “What are the Hyperscale capabilities”
notes.evidence: Autoscaling storage with support for up to 128 TB of database or 100 TB elastic pool size.

notes.front: Why are backups and restores fast in the Hyperscale service tier?
notes.back: They are based on file snapshots, which makes them nearly instantaneous.
notes.explanation: Because backup and restore use the storage layer, compute replicas carry less of the load.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Hyperscale service tier, “Back up and restore”
notes.evidence: Back up and restore operations for Hyperscale databases are file-snapshot based. This approach makes these operations nearly instantaneous. Because the Hyperscale architecture uses the storage layer for backup and restore, it reduces the processing burden and performance impact on compute replicas.

notes.front: A research institute expects one Azure SQL Database to grow to 90 terabytes and wants fast backups at that size. Which service tier fits?
notes.back: C: the Hyperscale service tier.
notes.choices:
A) An elastic pool of small databases
B) A logical server
C) The Hyperscale service tier
D) Point-in-time restore
notes.choicesExplained: A: a pool shares resources among many databases; it does not make one database larger. B: a logical server administers databases but sets no tier. D: that is a recovery feature, not a service tier.
notes.explanation: Hyperscale backups stay fast whatever the database size, and 90 terabytes is within its per-database limit.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): Hyperscale service tier, “What are the Hyperscale capabilities”
notes.evidence: Fast database backups (based on file snapshots) regardless of size with no I/O impact on compute resources.

notes.front: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines versus Managed Instance and SQL Database: which cloud service type is each?
notes.back: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is infrastructure as a service; Managed Instance and SQL Database are platform as a service.
notes.explanation: With a virtual machine you still manage the operating system and SQL Server; the two platform services automate updates, backups and recovery.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Compare Azure SQL services”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: A database team must apply operating system updates, configure the server and run backups themselves. Which Azure SQL option and cloud service type are they using?
notes.back: C: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines, which is infrastructure as a service.
notes.choices:
A) Azure SQL Database, platform as a service
B) Azure SQL Managed Instance, platform as a service
C) SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines, infrastructure as a service
D) Azure SQL Database, software as a service
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: both platform services automate updates, backups and recovery. D: Azure SQL Database is platform as a service, and it automates this work.
notes.explanation: Being responsible for the operating system and backups is the mark of infrastructure as a service; the platform services automate both.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Compare Azure SQL services”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: In Microsoft’s training comparison of Azure SQL services, which option shows the highest availability figure?
notes.back: Azure SQL Database, at 99.995%; the other two options show 99.99%.
notes.explanation: The training also says the service guarantees databases are available at least 99.995% of the time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Compare Azure SQL services”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
uses: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

notes.front: Before moving an on-premises SQL Server database to Azure SQL Database, a team wants to know which features will not work there. What should they run?
notes.back: C: Data Migration Assistant (DMA).
notes.choices:
A) Point-in-time restore
B) An elastic pool
C) Data Migration Assistant (DMA)
D) An auditing policy
notes.choicesExplained: A: it restores a database that is already in Azure. B: a pool shares resources; it tests nothing. D: auditing records database events once the database is running.
notes.explanation: It checks a database for compatibility issues that can affect how it works in Azure SQL Database.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, what does threat detection look for?
notes.back: Anomalous activities that indicate unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit a database.
notes.explanation: It watches continuously and alerts on things such as SQL injection attacks and unusual access patterns.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Advanced threat protection”
notes.evidence: This feature detects anomalous activities that indicate unusual and potentially harmful attempts to access or exploit your database. It continuously monitors your database for suspicious activities, and provides immediate security alerts on potential vulnerabilities, SQL injection attacks, and anomalous database access patterns.

notes.front: In Azure SQL Database, where does auditing write the database events it tracks?
notes.back: To an audit log in your Azure storage account.
notes.explanation: The log helps with regulatory compliance and with spotting anomalies that might mean a security problem.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Auditing for compliance and security”
notes.evidence: tracks database events and writes them to an audit log in your Azure storage account. Auditing can help you maintain regulatory compliance, understand database activity, and gain insight into discrepancies and anomalies that might indicate business concerns or suspected security violations.

notes.front: Which encryption does Azure SQL Database use for data in motion, at rest and in use?
notes.back: In motion: transport layer security. At rest: transparent data encryption. In use: Always Encrypted.
notes.explanation: Each state of the data gets its own protection, so data is covered while stored, travelling and being processed.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Data encryption”
notes.evidence: SQL Database helps secure your data by providing encryption. For data in motion, it uses transport layer security. For data at rest, it uses transparent data encryption. For data in use, it uses Always Encrypted.

notes.front: At 14:05 a developer accidentally deletes thousands of rows from an Azure SQL Database. The mistake is noticed at 15:00. What can recover the data as it was at 14:04?
notes.back: D: point-in-time restore.
notes.choices:
A) Threat detection
B) Data Migration Assistant (DMA)
C) Moving the database into an elastic pool
D) Point-in-time restore
notes.choicesExplained: B: it assesses databases before migration and restores nothing. C: pooling changes how resources are shared, not the data. A: it alerts on suspicious activity but cannot bring rows back.
notes.explanation: Any point within the automatic backup retention period can be recovered, including the minute before the mistake.
notes.source: Azure SQL docs (MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs): What is Azure SQL Database?, “Availability capabilities”
notes.evidence: All SQL Database deployment options support recovery to any point in time within the automatic backup retention period for any database.

notes.front: Which database engine does SQL database in Fabric use?
notes.back: The same SQL Database Engine as Azure SQL Database.
notes.explanation: It is Azure SQL Database’s engine, brought into Microsoft Fabric.
notes.source: Fabric docs (MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs): SQL database in Microsoft Fabric, “SQL database in Microsoft Fabric”
notes.evidence: A SQL database in Fabric uses the same SQL Database Engine as Azure SQL Database.

notes.front: Azure SQL Managed Instance versus Azure SQL Database: which is more compatible with on-premises SQL Server?
notes.back: Managed Instance, which is the better choice for moving existing solutions with advanced features and minimal changes.
notes.explanation: SQL Database supports most core database-level capabilities, but not all, so it suits new cloud applications better.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities, “Use cases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
